To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) observers can estimate the pose of objects with a precision that is sufficient for everyday tasks, (ii) the pose of the object's stick-like aspect can be seen more precisely than the pose of the slabs-like aspect, and (iii) the pose of an object can be estimated from a single binocular image, but the precision of such estimation is lower than when stereo and shading are also available.
observers are quite good at matching the pose of an object with a stick-like cross.
the pose of objects with aspect ratios 4:2 and 4:1 can be estimated with an accuracy of a few degrees.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the pose of objects is estimated from visual information.
the perception of 3-D object pose.
the question of what information is used for pose perception and how it is used.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pose of an object is perceived with high precision, but that the pose of the rim is perceived with higher precision than is the orientation of the principal axes.
the pose of an object's principal axes is perceived with a precision that is comparable to the precision with which subjects can match the orientation of a cross.

the pose of the spheroids is perceived with a precision of about 10º, and that this precision is influenced by the aspect ratios of the object, the type of cue, the presence of surface texture, and the presence of motion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the pose of the object's principal axes can be estimated with reasonable accuracy and that the pose of a stick-like aspect can be estimated with better accuracy than that of a slab-like aspect. © 2010 Elsevier Ltd.
observers can perceive the orientation of the principal axes in the 3-D shape of objects.
the pose of an object's principal axes is perceived with a standard deviation of a few degrees and that the estimation of tilt is more precise than the estimation of slant and roll.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pose of objects can be estimated quite precisely and that the precision is better for sticks than for slabs.
observers can estimate the pose of objects with high precision, and that the pose is seen as the pose of the object as a whole, rather than as the pose of individual parts.
the pose of an object can be perceived from contour, stereo, shading, and motion cues, though performance is best with the contour cue.
